claims.claim: The first full-scale Houdry catalytic cracking unit started at Sun Oil's Marcus Hook refinery in 1937 and processed 15,000 barrels per day.
claims.episode_span: In 1937 at Sun Oil’s Marcus Hook refinery, a new fixed-bed reactor began processing 15,000 barrels per day of gas oil.
claims.source_title: Houdry Process for Catalytic Cracking - National Historic Chemical Landmark
claims.supporting_quote: The first full-scale commercial catalytic cracker for the selective conversion of crude petroleum to gasoline went on stream at the Marcus Hook Refinery of Sun Company (now Sunoco, Inc.) in 1937.

claims.claim: Thermal cracking yielded about 25 percent gasoline while the Houdry process reached roughly 50 percent or 48 percent high-octane gasoline.
claims.episode_span: Where thermal cracking had converted roughly one-quarter of the feed into motor gasoline, the Houdry unit reached nearly half, and at higher octane.
claims.source_title: Houdry Process for Catalytic Cracking - National Historic Chemical Landmark
claims.supporting_quote: The Houdry process conserved natural oil by doubling the amount of gasoline produced by other processes.

claims.claim: Houdry units supplied a large share of 100-octane aviation gasoline for the Allies early in World War II.
claims.episode_span: Fourteen Houdry units supplied most of the 100-octane aviation gasoline used by the Allies in the early years of World War II.
claims.supporting_quote: By 1942, 14 Houdry fixed-bed catalytic units were bearing the unanticipated burden of producing high-octane aviation gasoline for the armed forces.
